طَرِيدٌ and ↓ مَطْرُودٌ (S, L, Msb) and ↓ مُطَرَّدٌ (A) [and ↓ مُطَّرَدٌ A man driven away, expelled, banished, or outcast; (L;) a man removed; put, or placed, at a distance, away, or far away: (S, L:) طَرِيدٌ is likewise applied to a female, as also طَرِيدَةٌ; and the pl. of both in this case is طَرَائِدُ. (M, L.) نَاقَةٌ طَرِيدٌ, without ة, means A she-camel driven away, and taken away: pl. طَرَائِدُ. (L.) ―
-b2- And (tropical:) One who is born after another: (S, L, K:) the second is termed the طَرِيد of the first. (S, L.) Also (assumed tropical:) One who is born before another. (K.) And hence, الطَّرِيدَانِ (tropical:) The night and the day: (A, L, K:) each being the طَرِيد of the other. (A, L.) ―
-b3- See also طَرَّادٌ. ―
-b4- Also (tropical:) Old; applied to a garment, or piece of cloth; syn. شَارِفٌ. (A, TA.) And ثَوْبٌ طَرَائِدُ is mentioned by Lh as meaning (assumed tropical:) An old, worn-out, garment, or piece of cloth. (TA.) ＝
-A2- And The base, or lower part, of the raceme of a palm-tree; (S, L, K;) as also ↓ طَرِيدَةٌ . (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
